data.role: Express 4 service using Prisma, Stripe and BullMQ; `npm start` runs src/server.js.
Process entry point: loads config, builds the app, starts the HTTP listener and the job worker.
Reads and validates DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET and REDIS_URL into one frozen config object.
Builds the Express app: JSON parsing, request logging, auth and the /api router.
Mounts the orders, products and webhooks routers under /api.
Verifies bearer JWTs and attaches req.user; rejects expired tokens with 401.
HTTP handlers for creating, listing and cancelling orders — a thin layer over orderService.
Order lifecycle: validates the cart, reserves stock, charges via Stripe and persists the order.
Reserves and releases stock. On release it looks up the owning order to restock each line item.
Wraps the Stripe SDK: creates payment intents and issues refunds.
Singleton Prisma client shared by every service.
Read-only catalogue endpoints with cursor pagination and live stock counts.
Verifies Stripe webhook signatures and marks orders paid or failed.
BullMQ worker that cancels unpaid orders after 30 minutes and releases their stock.
Maps thrown errors to JSON responses; hides stack traces outside development.
Data model: Product, Order, OrderItem and StockReservation.

data.issue: Circular dependency between orderService.js and inventoryService.js — each imports the other.
data.evidence: orderService.js imports reserveStock() from inventoryService.js, and inventoryService.js imports getOrderById() back from orderService.js to restock cancelled orders. inventoryService.js destructures that import at load time, so when orderService.js loads first — the normal path via routes/orders.js — it captures undefined. The first releaseStock() call, typically from the order-expiry job, throws "getOrderById is not a function". Moving the order lookup into a shared repository module breaks the cycle.
